q: What do we know about ds-clv-holdout-2021h1 in the customer-lifetime-value project?
a: It holds 318,400 accounts originated in 2021 H1, observed for 36 months through 2024-12, and is the test set for the CLV models (clv-oot-2021h1).

q: What came of the gross-versus-net CLV test exp-502 in the customer-lifetime-value project?
a: Netting expected credit losses cut the 36-month holdout value by 22% (gross $412, net $321 per account), which led to dec-clv-include-losses making finance CLV net of losses from August 2025.

q: What inputs does clv-ml-v2 in the customer-lifetime-value project use?
a: Offer-netted ARPU from feat-clv-arpu-v2, the retention hazard from feat-clv-hazard, plus tenure and the bureau-band loss rate; it is a LightGBM on net 36-month margin.

q: Which CLV model do finance and marketing use now in the customer-lifetime-value project?
a: clv-ml-v2, adopted by dec-clv-ship-ml-v2 for Q1 2026 reporting; it replaces clv-ml-v1, and the BG/NBD clv-bgnbd-v1 is kept only as a marketing sanity check.

q: What is the MAPE of clv-ml-v2 on the clv-oot-2021h1 holdout in the customer-lifetime-value project?
a: 15.2% MAPE on 36-month net margin, against 18.4% for clv-ml-v1 and 22.6% for the BG/NBD baseline.

q: Why does the customer-lifetime-value project's finance CLV now net expected credit losses?
a: Gross CLV overstated 36-month value by 22% on the 2021 H1 holdout (exp-502), so dec-clv-include-losses made the finance figure net of expected losses from August 2025.
